topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the cancer biology lecture series, its multidisciplinary audience, and the key learning outcomes for the session.

topics.label: Cellular and biological foundations of cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain cancer as a disease arising from genetic and epigenetic disruptions that cause failures in cellular differentiation and tissue architecture, alongside experimental models used to study these processes.

topics.label: Benign versus malignant tumors, invasion, and metastatic progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how tumors are distinguished as benign or malignant based on tissue invasion and metastasis, illustrated through histological features and stepwise progression.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature and classification rules
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the standard conventions and clinical exceptions used to name benign and malignant neoplasms based on their tissue of origin.

topics.label: Pathophysiological mechanisms of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the anatomical, functional, and systemic ways in which primary and metastatic tumors cause illness and death in patients.

topics.label: Comparative oncology and tumor incidence across species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore tumor incidence patterns across different human tissues and animal taxa, illustrating cancer as a universal consequence of multicellularity.

topics.label: Principles, histology, and modalities of cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the rationale, histological targets, and practical efficacy and limitations of screening programs across different cancer types.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical reminders
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by reviewing learning outcomes and reminding students about upcoming practical sessions and future lectures.
